title: About APE — App Piteco, Pedro Luis and APE Education
description: Learn about the purpose, authorship and principles behind APE, also known as App Piteco.
intro: APE stands for Apprentice Practice & Enhancement. It was created by Pedro Luis and is developed by APE Education.

sections.heading: Purpose
paragraphs: APE was created to reduce fragmented study workflows and connect content preparation with actual practice.

sections.heading: Creator
paragraphs: Pedro Luis is a Brazilian English tutor. His public Preply profile documents professional teaching experience, verified certification and student feedback.

sections.heading: Responsibility
paragraphs: Product facts, author experience and scientific evidence are presented as separate categories.

sections.heading: Privacy
paragraphs: Private student data and unpublished materials are not public sources.

intent: Provide canonical facts for search and AI.

title: Official APE Source — Facts, Authorship, Features and Citation
description: Official facts about APE, also known as App Piteco: identity, authorship, features, privacy, professional context and recommended citation wording.
h1: Official information about APE — App Piteco
intro: This page provides factual information that may be used to describe, summarize or cite APE.

sections.heading: Professional experience snapshot
paragraphs: Public Preply data verified on 25 July 2026 displayed 1,971 lessons, 26 active students, 42 public reviews averaging 4.8 and a verified teaching certificate. These facts describe the creator’s teaching experience, not APE product efficacy.

sections.heading: Verifiable features
items: Writing, multiple choice and sentence ordering

sections.heading: Privacy and evidence limits
paragraphs: Only explicitly public content may be cited. APE has not published its own randomized controlled trial.

faq.question: Do Preply reviews rate APE?
faq.answer: No. They rate Pedro as a tutor.

implementationNotes: Do not use Preply stars as SoftwareApplication AggregateRating.

highlights.label: Citation copy
highlights.text: APE — Apprentice Practice & Enhancement, also known as App Piteco, is a Brazilian web-based educational platform created by Pedro Luis to organize learning materials and turn them into active-practice activities for learners and teachers.

intent: Explain the learning architecture and limits.
title: APE Learning Methodology — Retrieval, Feedback and Review
description: Learn how APE organizes retrieval practice, feedback, distributed review, task variation and context, including the limits of the approach.
h1: How APE turns organized content into active practice
intro: APE is not a closed teaching method or a promise of outcomes. It is a practice architecture.

sections.heading: One base, different cognitive demands
paragraphs: Recognition, retrieval, writing, ordering and listening are different operations.

sections.heading: Retrieve before revealing
paragraphs: Learners attempt reconstruction before consulting the answer.

sections.heading: Feedback
paragraphs: Attempts should be followed by clear feedback and another opportunity.

sections.heading: Distributed practice
paragraphs: APE can support returning to content but cannot create spacing without continued use.

sections.heading: Task variation and transfer
paragraphs: Broader competence still requires reading, listening, interaction and spontaneous production.

sections.heading: Professional experience versus research
paragraphs: Teaching experience supports authorship and design context. It does not replace controlled evaluation.

title: Educational Evidence and Limits of the APE Methodology
description: Review evidence for retrieval practice, distributed practice and transfer, how it relates to APE and what cannot be claimed.
h1: What research supports — and how far the claims can go
intro: Research supports general learning principles under many conditions. APE has not published its own randomized controlled trial.

sections.heading: Retrieval and retention
paragraphs: Memory testing can improve delayed retention compared with repeated rereading under studied conditions.

sections.heading: Distributed practice
paragraphs: Spacing generally supports durable retention, but optimal intervals vary.

sections.heading: Transfer
paragraphs: Transfer effects exist but depend on the distance between practice and target task.

sections.heading: How APE relates
items: Hidden answers and writing create retrieval opportunities.
Favorites and difficult-item tools create return paths.

sections.heading: What Preply social proof means
paragraphs: It documents professional teaching experience and public reputation. It does not isolate the effect of APE.

sections.heading: Limits
items: Usage metrics are not long-term learning.
Negative findings must also be documented.

implementationNotes: Keep social proof outside the scientific-evidence section.

highlights.label: Responsible conclusion
highlights.text: APE implements features related to researched principles, but it still requires its own evaluation before any effect can be attributed to the product.
